slice_results.behavior_summary: When called (reached via save -> saveForm -> load -> getInit -> _load; module scope not reached in module), the code serializes an HTML form’s input elements into a URL-encoded string, then sends this serialized data via a POST request using fetch to a constructed URL, handling the response by invoking success or failure callbacks, enabling form data submission and server communication with error handling.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The analyzed code implements a standard pattern for serializing HTML form data and sending it via fetch to a server endpoint, with proper error handling and callbacks for success and failure. Unlike the known malicious patterns, it does not override native form submission methods, does not send data to hardcoded external attacker-controlled domains, and does not silently exfiltrate data. The URL used for fetch is constructed from internal variables (httpHandler.url and passed url parameters), indicating legitimate server communication rather than data theft. There is no obfuscation or suspicious manipulation of browser APIs. The code is consistent with typical client-side form submission and server interaction logic.

slice_meta.trigger: When called (reached via save -> saveForm -> load -> getInit -> _load; module scope not reached in module)

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, the code overrides HTMLFormElement.prototype.submit, intercepts form submissions, collects all form data, and sends it via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded external domain, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive user input.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code silently intercepts all form submissions and exfiltrates user-provided data to an external, attacker-controlled domain without user knowledge or consent. This is a direct data theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should not modify global browser prototypes to intercept user input or transmit sensitive data to third-party servers without explicit user consent and transparency.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some analytics or telemetry libraries may collect anonymized form usage data, but they do so with user consent, clear documentation, and do not exfiltrate raw form contents or credentials.
key_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript in main package file
Overrides HTMLFormElement.prototype.submit to intercept form submissions
Hardcoded external endpoint for data exfiltration (e.g., https://malicious-domain.com/collect)
Silent collection and transmission of all form data

execution_context.trigger: at runtime, when the malicious package is loaded in a web application and executed in the browser
execution_context.file_location: index.js or main JavaScript file of the malicious npm package
required_permissions: DOM access (to hook into HTML forms)

package_info.package_versions: various (dozens of malicious modules, specific versions not listed)
package_info.why_malicious: The IconBurst campaign distributed dozens of npm packages that were typosquats of popular modules. These packages contained obfuscated JavaScript code designed to intercept and exfiltrate sensitive form data from applications and websites that included them, enabling large-scale credential and data theft from unsuspecting users.

attack_chain.action: Malicious npm packages are published with names similar to popular packages (typosquatting) to trick developers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Developers accidentally install and include malicious packages in their projects.

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is included in downstream applications and websites, becoming part of the client-side codebase.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded and executed in end-user browsers.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript hooks into form submissions and exfiltrates all submitted form data to attacker-controlled domains.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive user data such as credentials and personally identifiable information (PII) from affected applications.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code that overrides or hooks HTMLFormElement.prototype.submit or addEventListener for form submission events
Presence of obfuscated or minified code that references fetch or XMLHttpRequest with external URLs
Unexpected network requests triggered during form submissions to domains not associated with the application
file_indicators: npm packages with names that are typosquats of popular modules (e.g., single-character changes, missing/extra letters)
Obfuscated JavaScript present in the main entry file (e.g., index.js) of the package
References to external domains in code strings within package files
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains not owned or operated by the application (e.g., https://malicious-domain.com/collect)
Network traffic to domains or endpoints associated with known supply chain attacks
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages with suspicious or typosquatted names during dependency audits. Analyze package contents for obfuscated code and modifications to HTMLFormElement.prototype.submit or form event handlers. Use runtime monitoring to detect unexpected outbound network requests from web applications, especially during form submissions, and flag any code that exfiltrates form data to untrusted or unknown domains.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, when the end function is called (directly or via fadeTo), the code serializes all form data on the page, encodes it as a hex string, and sends it via a non-blocking GET request to a hardcoded attacker-controlled URL, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive user input.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The function exfiltrates all form data to an external domain without user consent or any legitimate purpose, directly violating user privacy and data security.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: The legitimate end function in jQuery simply returns the previous object in the chain and should never perform network requests or access form data. Modifying this function to perform exfiltration is a clear abuse.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or telemetry might collect form data, but only with explicit user consent and never by modifying core library functions such as end.
key_indicators: Modification of a core library prototype function (jQuery.fn.end)
Network exfiltration of serialized form data via AJAX
Encoding of form data as a hex string in URL parameters
Hardcoded, attacker-controlled domains in the code

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, whenever jQuery's end or fadeTo is called in the browser
execution_context.file_location: jquery.min.js (or registration.min.js, icon.min.js, fontawesome.js, slim.js, all-min.js, etc.)

package_info.package_versions: 8.0.0 (and dozens of others, see report for full list)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a trojanized version of jQuery in which the 'end' prototype function is maliciously modified to exfiltrate all form data from the page to attacker-controlled domains whenever it is called, either directly or indirectly (e.g., via fadeTo). The package is distributed under many names and versions, often with additional suspicious files and unique exfiltration URLs, indicating a persistent, manually assembled supply chain attack targeting web applications.

attack_chain.action: User installs a malicious npm package containing a trojanized jQuery file (or similar).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in the project and loaded in the browser.

attack_chain.action: Trojanized jQuery is loaded and used in the web application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious prototype function (end) is available in the global jQuery object.

attack_chain.action: User or application code calls fadeTo or end (directly or indirectly), triggering the malicious end function.
attack_chain.leads_to: Form data is serialized and exfiltrated to attacker-controlled domains.

attack_chain.action: Injected scripts (from icons.js/min.js) load additional remote payloads (e.g., slim.js) from jsDelivr, which may contain further trojanized code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistence and further compromise of the web application.

behavioral_signatures: Modification of jQuery prototype functions (especially end) to perform network requests
Exfiltration of serialized form data via AJAX to external domains
Dynamic injection of remote scripts from non-standard or outdated sources
Presence of phony deprecation warnings in console output
file_indicators: jquery.min.js, registration.min.js, icon.min.js, fontawesome.js, slim.js, all-min.js (with non-standard or unexpected content)
Presence of termux.properties, npm cache, or npm logs in package tarballs
network_indicators: Requests to domains such as *.truex.biz.id, *.hanznesia.my.id, *.api-system.engineer, *.jsdelivr.net/gh/indexsc/libs/slim.js, and other listed campaign domains
AJAX GET requests with hex-encoded form data in query parameters
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan JavaScript dependencies for modifications to core library prototype functions (e.g., jQuery.fn.end). Flag any code that serializes and exfiltrates form data to external domains. Monitor for dynamic script injection from non-standard or outdated sources, and alert on requests to known campaign domains. Review package contents for unexpected files (e.g., termux.properties, npm logs) and non-standard file naming patterns. Correlate behavioral, file, and network indicators to identify supply chain attacks.

matched_knowledge.source_package: Boom! Mobile website (boom[.]us) Magecart skimmer (N/A (injected JavaScript on e-commerce website))

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At form submission, the code hooks the payment form's submit event, collects all entered payment and personal data, and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting form submissions and exfiltrating sensitive data to an untrusted external domain is a hallmark of web skimming (Magecart) attacks. The code operates silently, without user notification.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Payment forms should only submit data to the legitimate payment processor or backend, never to untrusted or undocumented third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate form data submission may occur to analytics or payment processors, but only to trusted, documented endpoints and never to suspicious or recently registered domains.
key_indicators: Event listener attached to payment form submission
Collection and serialization of all form data
Data exfiltration via HTTPS POST to suspicious domain (e.g., google-standard[.]com)
No user notification or consent for data transfer

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the user submits the payment form
execution_context.file_location: External JavaScript loaded from attacker domain (e.g., google-standard[.]com/sk.js)

package_info.why_malicious: The website was compromised by attackers who injected a malicious JavaScript skimmer. This script intercepts and exfiltrates payment card and private data entered by customers during checkout to attacker-controlled domains, constituting a classic Magecart attack targeting e-commerce transactions.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to the website and injects a malicious script tag with a Base64-encoded external source into the payment or checkout page.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious skimmer script is loaded and executed in the context of the checkout page.

attack_chain.action: The external skimmer script executes, hooks into the payment form's submit event, and collects user-entered payment and personal data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collected payment and personal data is prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The skimmer script sends the stolen payment and personal data to attacker-controlled domains via HTTPS POST requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credit card and personal information from compromised customers.

behavioral_signatures: Inline or external scripts loaded from non-standard, suspicious, or recently registered domains on payment or checkout pages
Base64-encoded script sources in HTML <script> tags
JavaScript code that hooks form submission events and sends collected data to external domains
file_indicators: References to domains such as google-standard[.]com, bing-analytics[.]com, google-money[.]com in script sources
Unexpected or unauthorized script tags present on payment or checkout pages
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains like google-standard[.]com, bing-analytics[.]com, google-money[.]com during checkout or payment form submission
Unusual network traffic to recently registered or non-canonical domains originating from payment pages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for <script> tags in HTML that load resources from suspicious or encoded sources, especially on payment or checkout pages. Inspect JavaScript for event listeners on forms that collect and send data to external domains. Use network monitoring to detect POST requests to known skimmer domains. Flag any new or unrecognized domains in script sources or network traffic, particularly those registered recently or not associated with the business. Correlate script injection events with anomalous network activity to identify active skimming.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, the code constructs a POST request to a hardcoded external server at http://95.216.251.178:8001/uploads, sending form data containing previously gathered sensitive information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of a hardcoded, non-legitimate server for data exfiltration is a strong indicator of malicious intent and is not required for DOM sanitization.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A DOM sanitization library should not communicate with unknown external servers or exfiltrate user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; legitimate libraries do not exfiltrate user data to arbitrary endpoints.
key_indicators: No user interaction or consent for data transmission

package_info.package_versions: all published versions (as of report time)
package_info.why_malicious: The package impersonates the trusted DOMPurify library and contains heavily obfuscated JavaScript code that, upon import or execution, steals sensitive data from the host system—including browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallet files, keychain data, and system identifiers—and exfiltrates this information to an attacker-controlled server via hardcoded network requests.

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated code is loaded and executed upon import or at runtime.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data collection from the host system

attack_chain.action: Harvest browser credentials by reading and decrypting browser profile data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive credentials are prepared for exfiltration

attack_chain.leads_to: Wallet data is prepared for exfiltration

Exfiltrate all collected data to the attacker's server via HTTP POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive data; compromise complete

behavioral_signatures: Access to browser profile directories and 'Login Data' SQLite files
Decryption of browser-stored credentials using system APIs
Access to cryptocurrency wallet directories such as ~/.electrum and ~/.bitcoin
Obfuscated code with dynamic variable and function names
Outbound HTTP POST requests to hardcoded, non-standard endpoints
file_indicators: Access to files like 'Login Data' in browser profile directories

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript packages that access browser profile or wallet directories, especially those that read and decrypt 'Login Data' files or access ~/.electrum and ~/.bitcoin. Flag any package making HTTP POST requests to unknown or hardcoded endpoints, particularly http://95.216.251.178:8001/uploads. Use static and dynamic analysis to detect obfuscated code and dynamic variable/function name generation. Alert on any package that exfiltrates system information or sensitive files to external servers.

matched_knowledge.source_package: polyfill.io (CDN service) (CDN (not a package manager, but a third-party JavaScript CDN service))

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, the code could attach event listeners to form submissions, intercept submitted form data, and exfiltrate it to an attacker-controlled endpoint via network requests, resulting in potential theft of user credentials or sensitive information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating form data is a hallmark of formjacking attacks. This behavior is highly suspicious and never expected from a polyfill service, as it directly compromises user privacy and security.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Polyfill scripts should not interact with user input, monitor form submissions, or exfiltrate data to external endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate form analytics or error tracking may collect form data, but only with explicit user consent and transmission to trusted, well-known domains. They do not operate covertly or send data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
key_indicators: Form event interception via addEventListener on form elements
Network exfiltration of user-submitted data to untrusted endpoints
Use of attacker-controlled domains for data collection

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user visits a website that includes cdn.polyfill.io.

package_info.package_manager: CDN (not a package manager, but a third-party JavaScript CDN service)
package_info.package_versions: All versions served after February 2024 (post-acquisition by Funnull)
package_info.why_malicious: After its acquisition by Funnull in February 2024, the polyfill.io CDN service began serving malicious, obfuscated JavaScript payloads. These payloads inject unwanted redirects, selectively target mobile users, evade detection through delayed execution and environment checks, and can potentially exfiltrate user data. The code is dynamically generated and adapts its behavior, turning every website that includes cdn.polyfill.io into a potential supply chain attack vector.

attack_chain.action: A website includes a script tag referencing cdn.polyfill.io, causing the browser to load and execute the malicious JavaScript payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the user's browser environment.

attack_chain.action: The malicious JavaScript checks for mobile devices, admin or analytics presence, and delays execution to evade detection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Selective targeting of victims and evasion of security tools or manual analysis.

attack_chain.action: If targeting conditions are met, the code injects a script from a typo-squatted analytics domain or performs redirects to malicious sites.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is redirected to attacker-controlled content or further malicious payloads are loaded.

attack_chain.action: Potential for further attacks such as formjacking or data exfiltration if the payload evolves or is updated.
attack_chain.leads_to: Possible theft of user data, credentials, or sensitive information.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript payloads served from cdn.polyfill.io
Dynamic script injection from typo-squatted analytics domains (e.g., www.googie-anaiytics.com)
Conditional logic based on user agent, admin or analytics presence
Delayed execution using setTimeout before performing malicious actions
Unexpected redirects to non-legitimate or attacker-controlled domains
Potential interception and exfiltration of form data
file_indicators: References to https://www.googie-anaiytics.com/gtags.js in dynamically injected scripts
Obfuscated inline JavaScript with dynamic script injection logic
network_indicators: Redirects to domains associated with sports betting, pornography, or other malicious content
Potential future exfiltration to attacker-controlled endpoints (e.g., https://attacker.example/collect)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan website source code and network traffic for references to cdn.polyfill.io and typo-squatted analytics domains such as www.googie-anaiytics.com. Monitor for obfuscated JavaScript payloads that perform delayed execution, dynamic script injection, or conditional redirects. Use web application firewalls and browser security tools to block or alert on unexpected script sources and outbound requests to known malicious domains. Regularly audit third-party scripts and replace cdn.polyfill.io with trusted alternatives. Monitor for suspicious form data exfiltration to untrusted endpoints.
